messages:
maria_cs: Heads-up — ACME reported a regression: rerank endpoint v1/score now gives different scores for the exact same payload after the model rollout this morning. Customer sees rank flip for top-3 results.

maria_cs: Minimal repro from the customer (they say input is identical):
```json
{
  "query": "cheap bluetooth headphones",
  "candidates": ["Brand A model X", "Brand B model Y", "Brand C model Z"],
  "top_k": 3
}
```

maria_cs: Expected stable scores across deployments; observed: [0.82, 0.79, 0.65] before rollout -> [0.76, 0.81, 0.66] after. Customer upset, says this affects UI.

jordan_support: Can you paste the request_id from their failing call and the timestamps? Need to correlate logs. Also are they on Dedicated or Hosted?

maria_cs: Request id: req_0a9f3b. Customer on Hosted (standard prod cluster, us-west). They first saw issue at 2026-03-17T09:12:05Z.

anil_ml: Thanks. Quick hypotheses: model artifact changed (different tokenizer/normalization), or a rollout introduced a variant with precision/quant differences. Another possibility: inference batching or left-padding differences causing attention mask shuffles for short sequences.

sam_engineer: I pulled logs for req_0a9f3b — model variant served: rwd-llama2-13b-q4f_v2. Deploy timestamp 2026-03-17T08:50:12Z. Kernel config shows batch_size cap=8.

sam_engineer: Customer supplied candidate ordering; our reranker scores should be order-invariant. If batching groups requests with different pad lengths we could see non-determinism if KV cache indexing bug exists.

deploy-bot: Deployment rwd-llama2-13b-q4f_v2 promoted to prod at 2026-03-17T08:50:12Z by @ci-pipeline. Canary policy: 15%.

lee_sre: Canary was rolled from 15% -> 100% at 2026-03-17T08:54:30Z after health checks passed. No immediate error spikes in infra metrics. CPU/GPU util normal.

anil_ml: Request a deterministic repro from our infra: run the exact customer payload against the previous model artifact (pre-rollout) and the new one in a controlled, single-request mode (no batching). If scores diverge, we have a model-level change. If they match when single-requested but diverge under load, it's a serving bug.

maria_cs: I asked the customer for a short corpus of 10 queries and candidate sets (they sent it). They said they can tolerate a quick maintenance window for us to run tests.

sam_engineer: Repro steps I ran locally (single request):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"query":"cheap bluetooth headphones","candidates":["Brand A model X","Brand B model Y","Brand C model Z"],"top_k":3}'
```
Observed (single-request, no batching) with rwd-llama2-13b-q4f_v1: [0.823,0.789,0.652]
Observed with rwd-llama2-13b-q4f_v2 (single-request): [0.821,0.789,0.652] — minor diff but ordering stable.

sam_engineer: Then I reproduced under load (batching on) with 16 concurrent requests to force batching: v1 -> [0.823,0.789,0.652], v2 -> [0.762,0.813,0.655] — matches customer's report. So the delta appears only when requests are batched.

anil_ml: That suggests a batching-induced state bug. Likely root causes: (1) index misalignment when assembling KV caches across candidates, (2) pad/truncate inconsistency between tokenizer versions, or (3) shared buffer reuse without proper reset.

lee_sre: I traced the runtime logs for the batch containing req_0a9f3b. There's a WARN: "kv-cache-offset mismatch detected" at 08:52:17 but no error-level crash. Attaching excerpt:
```
[08:52:17] WARN runtime/kv_cache.go:122 kv-cache-offset mismatch: batch_idx=7 expected=0 got=64 request=req_0a9f3b
```

maria_cs: Customer is asking for ETA and rollback. They said feature is high priority for them.

jordan_support: Recommend temporary mitigation: pin the customer to rwd-llama2-13b-q4f_v1 (previous artifact) while we investigate. Also offer credit for incident.

sam_engineer: I can open a hotfix: disable cross-request batching for rerank route by default (set batch_size=1) until we patch the KV cache handling. Impact: small latency increase, cost up. Need approvals.

anil_ml: Agree. Also add unit tests for batched KV cache offsets and tokenization parity between v1/v2 artifacts.

lee_sre: I'll coordinate rollback for VIP tenants. If we pin only ACME to v1 we'll do a traffic rule mapping. I can enact that in the afternoon window.

maria_cs: Action items: Sam -> implement temp disable batching pr by EOD (owner: @sam_engineer). Anil -> root-cause analysis on model runtime changes + tests (owner: @anil_ml). Lee -> prepare customer pin/rollback plan (owner: @lee_sre). I'll notify ACME and schedule maintenance.

jordan_support: Thanks. Please post progress here and paste PR + runbook links. :thumbsup:

maria_cs: Noted. I'll update the thread once customer confirms the maintenance window.
_notes: thread follows agents.md schema: single continuous messages string prefixed by sender names
